newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX in fresh plunge, tracking Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: German DAX in fresh plunge, tracking Wall Street.

text.p: Blue chip German shares suffered a renewed sell-off on Thursday as nerves remained on edge after fresh declines on Wall Street and investors braced themselves to see what the afternoon would bring.
"It's just nerves, nerves and more nerves here," said a Frankfurt trader. "There is no hope of us decoupling from the U.S."
The 30-share DAX was down 103.43 points, or more than three percent, at 3,198.13 points in early floor trade, just under a key technical support level at 3,200.
But the extent of the decline on Thursday was deceptive as the market had already priced in much of Wall Street's weakness in late trade on Wednesday.
The IBIS DAX index, which reflects all-day trade in DAX shares, was down a more modest 12.13 points at 3,198.81 points.
June DTB DAX futures were down four points at 3,211.
Dow Jones Industrials fell 94 points to 6,517 points on Wednesday, to end up eight percent off their closing high of March 11.
Dealers said that while German shares should not be tracking the U.S. on the basis of economic fundamentals, the psychological impact of Wall Street's decline was immense.
"It's clear we are at a different stage here in the economic cycle -- no-one is talking about a German rate hike today. But it still all depends on Wall Street," a dealer said.
The DAX was seen hovering about the 3,200 point level amid thin trading volumes thought the day.
The Bundesbank's policy-making meeting would attract its usual measure of attention but economists were not expecting the central bank to make any move on rates.
